context.exploration_scope: Went one level deeper than PHASE-S28: checked whether the foundation model's own declared references actually resolve, and traced Experience->Signal->Principle->Decision->Outcome connectivity for both adopted Principles -- checked reusability first for any finding, built nothing regardless of outcome

problem: PHASE-S28 confirmed the foundation exists, is unduplicated, and its production_goals_mapping is accurate -- but never checked whether the foundation model's OWN internal citations (the specific files and principle IDs it names as evidence for its core_relationships) actually resolve. A citation that looks plausible but does not resolve is a real, if narrow, gap in the foundation's actual composition, distinct from whether the foundation exists at all.

Underlying capability already covered by adopted principle_goal_production_runtime_successful_resolution_ssi_s4_v1: true. Both Principle lifecycles connected end-to-end: true. 0 new structure/Architecture, 0 existing artifacts modified, 0 synthetic change/Experience, 0 CI wiring, 0 automatic policy, 0 automatic execution. Verdict: MINIMAL_GAP_DEFINED.

action.action_summary: Resolved every reference the foundation model itself declares (3 ingestion-channel example_refs against the canonical Experience Layer, the chain-lens source file, and the boundary relationship's two source components) against real, current records; found the PRIN-001/E23 citation does not resolve as stated; checked reusability first by confirming the real underlying capability is already covered by the adopted, operationally-ready SSI-S4 Principle; traced Experience->Signal->Principle->Decision->Outcome connectivity for both Principle lifecycles.

evidence.evidence_detail: final_state=MINIMAL_GAP_DEFINED, failed_checks=boundary_references_resolve, prin_001_citation_accurate=false, underlying_capability_covered=true, regression_all_passed=true, dangling=0, duplicates=0

result.note: Found one narrow, non-functional gap (citation_accuracy_only): the foundation model's PRIN-001/E23 citation does not resolve as stated, but the real capability it names is already fully covered by the adopted PHASE-SSI-S4 Principle -- recorded as exactly that scope, not inflated into a capability gap, and not remediated here.

cause.root_cause_summary: A foundation model built by citing several real, separately-generated phases (S10, S11, E23, S18) is only as accurate as each of those individual citations -- PRIN-001 was a real, consistently-used informal label across PHASE-E36/E38/E40/E44 describing a real, already-adopted capability (later formalized as the SSI-S4 Principle), but it was never itself registered in E23, so citing it as "(E23)" was inaccurate even though the underlying concept it named was completely real and already covered elsewhere.

lesson: Checking whether a foundation's own citations resolve is a different, necessary check from checking whether the foundation exists -- and reusability has to be checked FIRST when a citation fails: the honest question is not just "does this reference resolve" but "is the real thing it was trying to name already covered somewhere else," because conflating a citation-accuracy issue with a missing-capability gap would have wrongly justified building something that already exists.
